title: SDK adaptive envelope shrinking and realtime compatibility scoring for telemetry
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Summary: Reduce telemetry ingestion cost and improve forward/backward compatibility by shipping an SDK-side "adaptive envelope" that emits a compact, versioned telemetry envelope with optional-field hints and a lightweight compatibility_score header. The server ingestion pipeline will consume the envelope, apply safe server-side enrichments/transformations, and record compatibility metrics for rollback decisions.

Background: SDK telemetry payloads have grown organically (extra context fields, nested traces, large metadata maps). This increases network cost, ingestion CPU, S3 storage, and downstream ETL complexity. Current ingestion accepts many ad-hoc fields but lacks a reliable schema version header and no realtime signal about how well the client matches the server's expected contract. We need an approach that: (1) lets SDKs emit smaller payloads by omitting optional fields safely; (2) keeps servers able to rehydrate or map older envelopes to new analytics tables; (3) provides realtime compatibility signals during rollouts.

Design proposal:
- SDK changes: introduce envelope.version (semver-ish string) and envelope.hints (list of omitted optional fields with reason codes). SDK computes a compatibility_score (0-100) locally by comparing its available fields to a minimal 'required' fingerprint baked into the SDK and periodically refreshed from the server via a small metadata endpoint. The SDK will also run adaptive envelope shrinking: when running over constrained networks or when per-event size exceeds a configured threshold, it will remove lower-priority optional fields and add corresponding hints.
- Ingest changes: ingestion-gateway will accept envelope.version and hints, run a lightweight validation, and write raw envelope+hints to a short-term staging topic. A schema-transform worker will apply versioned transformation rules to map older envelopes into the canonical analytic schema. Transform rules are stored in a versioned ruleset service with a simple DSL (examples in design doc). We will emit compatibility metrics to the console: percent of events per version, average compatibility_score, failure rate, and transformation lossiness.
- Rollout strategy: server-side transforms will be enabled by default; adopt canary rollout with 1% -> 10% -> 50% phased ingestion traffic. During canary we will run parallel acceptance: transform+store versus raw-store and compute diffs on key metrics to detect data loss. We will provide a client upgrade cadence: force-minor only after transformation coverage >= 99.5% and compatibility_score median >= 90.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We favor server-side transforms over forcing immediate SDK upgrades to preserve customer experience. This increases operational complexity (transform rules) but reduces broken-event risk.
- Local compatibility scoring increases SDK complexity and network metadata churn but gives early warning of mismatches.
- Storing hints verbatim increases index size slightly but is critical for debugging and for future automated rule learning.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field but high-level: SDKs emit version+hints; ingestion accepts new envelope shape; transform worker maps >=99.5% of production events during canary; dashboards show compatibility metrics; no increase in 95th percentile ingest latency beyond 10%.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Adaptive+Envelope+Design
- Prototype PR (SDK): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-sdk/pull/213
- Ingest worker prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-ingest/pull/421
- Transform rules repo (examples): https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-transforms/tree/main/examples
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/telemetry/adaptive-envelope-canary

Open questions: list of fields and rank for 'optional' classification; how often the SDK should refresh server fingerprint metadata; fallback policy when compatibility_score < 40 (drop vs send raw large envelope).

Next steps: finish SDK tests and sampling harness (Aisha), wire transform ruleset service and unit tests (Sam), prepare canary dashboard alerts and runbook (SRE), propose update to client upgrade cadence in PM review (Jasmin).

acceptance_criteria: SDKs publish envelope.version and envelope.hints for every telemetry event
Ingestion gateway accepts new envelope fields with zero dropped events in canary window
Transform worker maps >= 99.5% of canary events to canonical schema with lossiness < 0.05%
Compatibility dashboards show median compatibility_score >= 90 during canary
No more than 10% increase in 95th percentile ingest latency compared to baseline
